name: mem_fs
description: Start MemProcFS on a memory image for the length of one call, do one thing with the file tree it mounts, and stop it: the mount is gone when the call returns, so nothing later can read it; what survives is the files an export wrote and the engine's own stdout and stderr, kept as files beside the mount. SENSITIVE: memory can hold anything the machine held (command lines, environments, keys, process pages), so mode text and mode export, which write content, run only as a job and only with write_values: true, and write only to $OUT/mem_fs (mode 0600, created exclusively, never over an existing file); outside a job they are refused before MemProcFS starts. The tool cannot see whether the job was run with secret_output: true, which seals the output as sensitive: run it that way. The answer is a locator (virtual path, output file, size, status per item) with no content and no digest; sizes and sha256 are in $OUT/mem_fs/export-manifest.jsonl. mode list shows names, kinds and sizes of a directory, no content. mode export copies the named virtual files byte for byte (never as text, never inside JSON); mode text writes one file only if it is UTF-8 text with no NUL byte, and refuses anything else instead of decoding it with replacements. A file over max_bytes_per_path is not exported and is counted; an item that could not be exported says why and complete is false. One deadline (timeout_seconds) holds over startup, reads and export, and a failure names the phase (startup, read, export, cleanup); the engine is then stopped and unmounted. A virtual path that resolves outside the mount (a link) is refused for that item, and a link loop or any other failure is that item's status; the other items go on, and the counts add up to the ones requested. Whether MemProcFS contacts a symbol server is governed by the job's network policy (a job has no network unless it asks for the run's allowlist); this tool passes MemProcFS no flag about it, and the pinned binary's behaviour in that respect was not verified in this review. It needs MemProcFS, /dev/fuse the process can open and fusermount3 or fusermount, which a sandbox may not provide: the answer says which of these the host has. It mounts, exports and measures nothing else: it does not say what a file means, that a region is complete or that a page was resident, and which virtual paths exist depends on the MemProcFS version and the image (list first).

mount.description: Where to mount it: a directory under your own work/<your id>/ (in a job, under $OUT); it must be empty. The engine's two log files are written beside it and kept

mode.description: list (default): names, kinds and sizes. text: one UTF-8 text file written to $OUT/mem_fs. export: the files in paths, byte for byte, to $OUT/mem_fs. text and export need write_values and a job

list.description: A path inside the mount: the directory to list (default: the mount's root) or, with mode text, the one file to write out

paths.description: With mode export: the virtual files to copy (at most 1000), relative paths inside the mount

write_values.description: Write memory content to files (default false). Required by text and export, and refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; the answer never carries content

max_bytes_per_path.description: Do not export a file larger than this (default 4294967296); it is counted and named, not cut. Raise it to export a larger file

limit.description: Entries or items shown inline (default 200); all are counted, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in complete_results

timeout_seconds.description: One deadline for startup, reads and export (default 300, at least 2); unmounting after it has its own bounded wait
